It fetches source code from the official GitHub repository (menloresearch/jan.git) pinned to a specific tag (v0.8.4) with SHA-256 checksum verification. data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model returned 'inconclusive' solely because it encountered an HTTP 400 error when reviewing .gitignore, not because of any security concern. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified the package as safe. The openrouter/free report is advisory-only (advisory: true) and also failed due to a parse error. There is no actual security disagreement between the models.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore due to HTTP 400 API error
openrouter/free model failed to parse PKGBUILD response and only reviewed 1 of 3 files
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parse errors) should not block the overall security verdict when critical files like PKGBUILD are successfully reviewed and found safe

The audit tool should distinguish between 'file could not be reviewed due to tool error' and 'file has inconclusive security status' - a .gitignore file that fails to parse should not make the entire package 'inconclusive'

For inherently safe files like .gitignore and .SRCINFO that contain no executable code, tool errors should be logged but should not override successful reviews of security-critical files like PKGBUILD
